title: The Work Lifecycle: Expected vs Ceiling vs Actual
summary: WLU distinguishes between the expected work, the admitted hard ceiling, and the actual spent work.
why: Allows for cautious admission (ceilings) while maintaining accurate reporting of real work performed.
invariants: expectedMicroWlu: the predicted work for a demand.
ceilingMicroWlu: the hard admitted work limit before top-up is required.
Actual WLU: the only amount that becomes 'spent' at settlement.
Unused ceiling is released at settlement; it is never spent.
evidence_note: Source: oorexx_work_load_units_v0.12/README.md:52-66. Line 65: 'At settlement, only actual work becomes spent WLU. Unused ceiling is released.'
